statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-120967 lets a remote client bypass client certificate verification when nginx requires client certificates (ssl_verify_client on) in a non-default stream virtual server selected by SNI. nginx.org lists 1.25.5 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163934. The fix makes ngx_stream_ssl_handler() re-read the stream SSL server configuration after the handshake, before it checks the client certificate: commit 77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 on the stable-1.30 branch (1.30.7) and commit 6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559 in 1.31.9, https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 and https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559. Every nginx-mainline package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI repository (1.28.2-r0 and 1.29.5-r0 to 1.29.8-r9 on x86_64 and aarch64, and 1.29.4-r0 on aarch64 only) is an empty package, with an installed size of 0 in the repository index, that depends only on the nginx package of the same version, so it carries no nginx code of its own. That nginx package is affected up to 1.29.8-r7 and fixed in 1.29.8-r9. Pending: whether this owner, which never contains nginx code, should be recorded as not containing the component, or should follow the nginx build it depends on, which would make 1.29.8-r9 its first fixed build.

CVE-2026-120967 lets a remote client bypass client certificate verification when nginx requires client certificates (ssl_verify_client on) in a non-default stream virtual server selected by SNI. nginx.org lists 1.25.5 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163934. The fix makes ngx_stream_ssl_handler() re-read the stream SSL server configuration after the handshake, before it checks the client certificate: commit 77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 on the stable-1.30 branch (1.30.7) and commit 6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559 in 1.31.9, https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 and https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559. For Alpine 3.24, DHI builds nginx-mainline from the upstream nginx releases. We read every nginx-mainline package published for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI repository, 1.29.8-r0 to 1.31.9-r6 on x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against the index checksum. 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1 contain no files and depend on the nginx package of the same version, which is vulnerable. 1.31.2-r2 to 1.31.8-r5 ship nginx 1.31.2 to 1.31.8, configured with --with-stream=dynamic and --with-stream_ssl_module, and 1.31.9-r5 and 1.31.9-r6 ship nginx 1.31.9. In each of these builds we disassembled the stream SSL handler in ngx_stream_module.so, located by its calls to ngx_ssl_handshake and SSL_get_verify_result: in 1.31.9-r5 and 1.31.9-r6 it reloads the server configuration after a handshake that completes on the first call, before it tests whether client verification is on, as the fix does, on both architectures, and in every build from 1.31.2-r2 to 1.31.8-r5 it tests the configuration it loaded before the handshake. The 1.31.2 to 1.31.8 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable, so the range ends at 1.31.9-r5, the first nginx-mainline build of 1.31.9.

CVE-2026-120967 lets a remote client bypass client certificate verification when nginx requires client certificates (ssl_verify_client on) in a non-default stream virtual server selected by SNI. nginx.org lists 1.25.5 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163934. The fix makes ngx_stream_ssl_handler() re-read the stream SSL server configuration after the handshake, before it checks the client certificate: commit 77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 on the stable-1.30 branch (1.30.7) and commit 6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559 in 1.31.9, https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 and https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559. For Alpine 3.23, DHI builds nginx from Alpine's 3.23 nginx package recipe, with the upstream 1.28 or 1.29 release. Alpine backported this fix in its 1.28.3-r8 package: https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/nginx/APKBUILD. DHI release numbers differ from Alpine's: the DHI 1.28.3-r9 build sorts above Alpine's 1.28.3-r8 but was built on 2026-08-03, before the backport, and does not carry it. The first DHI builds that include the backport are 1.28.3-r11 and 1.29.8-r9, published on 2026-11-23. We read every nginx build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI repository, 1.28.0-r8 to 1.28.3-r11 and 1.29.4-r0 to 1.29.8-r9 on x86_64 and aarch64, with 1.28.1-r0 and 1.29.4-r0 published for aarch64 only, each checked against the index checksum. Each nginx binary reports an upstream release in the vulnerable range and is configured with --with-stream=dynamic and --with-stream_ssl_module. We disassembled the stream SSL handler in ngx_stream_module.so from the nginx-mod-stream package of each build (nginx-mod-stream is published for every build except x86_64 1.28.3-r4 and 1.29.7-r0), located by its calls to ngx_ssl_handshake and SSL_get_verify_result: in 1.28.3-r11 and 1.29.8-r9 it reloads the server configuration after a handshake that completes on the first call, before it tests whether client verification is on, as the fix does, on both architectures, and in every earlier build it tests the configuration it loaded before the handshake. Every 1.28 build sorts below every 1.29 build, so the fixed 1.28.3-r11 sorts below the unfixed 1.29 builds and the range has two spans: builds before 1.28.3-r11 are affected, 1.28.3-r11 is fixed, the 1.29 builds from 1.29.4-r0 to 1.29.8-r7 are affected, and 1.29.8-r9 is fixed.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-120967 lets a remote client bypass client certificate verification when nginx requires client certificates (ssl_verify_client on) in a non-default stream virtual server selected by SNI. nginx.org lists 1.25.5 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163934. The fix makes ngx_stream_ssl_handler() re-read the stream SSL server configuration after the handshake, before it checks the client certificate: commit 77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 on the stable-1.30 branch (1.30.7) and commit 6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559 in 1.31.9, https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 and https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559. Every nginx build published for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI repository (1.28.3-r0 on aarch64 only, and 1.28.3-r1, 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.30.3-r1, 1.30.3-r2, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1 on x86_64 and aarch64), each checked against the index checksum, ships an upstream release in the vulnerable range, configured with --with-stream=dynamic and --with-stream_ssl_module, with no backport of the fix. We disassembled the stream SSL handler in ngx_stream_module.so from the nginx-mod-stream package of each build, located by its calls to ngx_ssl_handshake and SSL_get_verify_result: in every build it tests the configuration it loaded before the handshake. The 1.31.2 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable. No fixed build is published for this owner; for Alpine 3.24 the fixed upstream releases are published under the package names nginx-stable and nginx-mainline instead.

CVE-2026-120967 lets a remote client bypass client certificate verification when nginx requires client certificates (ssl_verify_client on) in a non-default stream virtual server selected by SNI. nginx.org lists 1.25.5 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163934. The fix makes ngx_stream_ssl_handler() re-read the stream SSL server configuration after the handshake, before it checks the client certificate: commit 77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 on the stable-1.30 branch (1.30.7) and commit 6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559 in 1.31.9, https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/77f90f1c0cbf79145e5667b7e171f8766ccb6765 and https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/6f9fceed8dd7eb7d39b3930dc4f6824ecfe88559. Debian fixes it for trixie in 1.26.3-3+deb13u11, DSA-6642-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-120967. Debian lists 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 and earlier trixie revisions as vulnerable. The fixed version in this range is the DHI rebuild of 1.26.3-3+deb13u11, the first nginx build in the DHI Debian repository made from that revision; the earlier builds there are rebuilds of 1.26.3-3+deb13u9 and 1.26.3-3+deb13u10. The Debian changelog shipped in the fixed build lists the backport, 'verify stream client certificates using the server configuration selected by SNI'. We checked the fixed build and the 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 rebuild on amd64 and arm64, each package against its index checksum; /usr/sbin/nginx in both is configured with --with-stream=dynamic and --with-stream_ssl_module. We compared /usr/lib/nginx/modules/ngx_stream_module.so in the libnginx-mod-stream package, read through the symbols of the matching libnginx-mod-stream-dbgsym package: in the fixed build ngx_stream_ssl_handler reloads the ngx_stream_ssl_module server configuration after ngx_ssl_handshake succeeds and before it tests the verify setting, while in the 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 rebuild it tests the configuration loaded before the handshake, on both architectures. Each binary was matched to its debug symbols by build ID.
